searches.answer: Kubernetes 1.20 will deprecate Docker runtime support, with the removal planned for version 1.22. This change is due to Docker runtime's non-compliance with the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) for Kubernetes. Kubernetes platforms like Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Red Hat OpenShift have already moved to default container runtimes such as containerd or CRI-O. Docker Desktop release notes indicate updates to Kubernetes, cri-dockerd, CNI plugins, containerd, runc, and Go, with Kubernetes version 1.34.3 as of 2026-03-02. Kubernetes support for Docker via dockershim was removed in v1.20, and users are advised to switch to other compliant container runtimes like containerd or CRI-O.

results.title: Container Runtimes | Kubernetes
results.content:
#### Note:

Kubernetes releases before v1.24 included a direct integration with Docker Engine, using a component named dockershim. That special direct integration is no longer part of Kubernetes (this removal was announced as part of the v1.20 release). You can read Check whether Dockershim removal affects you to understand how this removal might affect you. To learn about migrating from using dockershim, see Migrating from dockershim.
